problems.title: An incomplete frequency table cannot describe twelve rolls
problems.question: A die is said to be rolled 12 times. The table lists outcomes 1,3,4,5,6 with relative frequencies 1/6,1/6,1/6,1/3,1/12. Find the mean, range, median, mode and standard deviation.
problems.idea: Check that relative frequencies sum to one before treating the table as complete.
steps: The listed relative frequencies sum to 11/12, corresponding to counts 2,2,2,4,1: only 11 rolls. Their value sum is 42 and squared-value sum is 188.
For these 11 recorded values alone, the mean is 42/11, the range is 6-1=5, the median is 4, and the mode is 5. The standard deviation is √(188/11-(42/11)²)=4√19/11.
If an unlisted twelfth outcome is k∈{1,...,6}, the full mean is (42+k)/12 and its standard deviation is √[(188+k²)/12-((42+k)/12)²].
For every such completion the range stays 5 and mode stays 5. The full median is 4 if k≤4 and 4.5 if k=5 or 6.
problems.answer: The printed table is incomplete. Range=5 and mode=5 are fixed; the full mean, median and standard deviation require the missing roll.
problems.note: The frequencies total 11/12 rather than 1. If the missing outcome was intended to be 2, the completed mean is 11/3, median 4 and standard deviation √23/3, but the source does not state that missing frequency.

problems.title: Which symmetry axes are not diagonals?
problems.question: A regular polygon has interior-angle sum 2160°. How many of its symmetry axes are not diagonals?
problems.idea: Find its number of sides, then distinguish the two kinds of axes for an even-sided polygon.
formulas: Interior-angle sum=(n-2)180°; a regular even n-gon has n/2 vertex-pair axes and n/2 side-midpoint axes.
steps: Seven symmetry axes join opposite vertices and contain diagonals.
The other seven join opposite side midpoints and are not diagonals.

problems.title: Two applications of independent-event probability
problems.question: A,B are independent. (a) Find P(A∪B) if P(A)=0.4,P(B)=0.5. (b) Find P(A∩B) if P(A∪B)=7/9 and P(A)=2P(B).
problems.idea: Use independence to replace the intersection with a product.
steps: (b) Let P(B)=t and P(A)=2t. Then 3t-2t²=7/9.
This gives 18t²-27t+7=(3t-1)(6t-7)=0. Only t=1/3 has both t and 2t in [0,1].
The intersection is 2t²=2/9.

problems.title: Reflections, translation and composition
problems.question: Let f be reflection in the y-axis, g reflection in the origin, and h(x,y)=(2x,y-1). (a) Find the separate images of A(2,1). (b) Find (h∘g∘f)(a,b).
problems.idea: Apply each rule in the specified order.
formulas: f(x,y)=(-x,y); g(x,y)=(-x,-y); composition h∘g∘f applies f first.
steps: For A, the separate images are f(A)=(-2,1),g(A)=(-2,-1),h(A)=(4,0).
For the composition: (a,b)→(-a,b)→(a,-b)→(2a,-b-1).
The formula for h scales x by 2 as well as changing y; apply the printed rule directly.

problems.title: Exam probabilities need an independence assumption
problems.question: Three students pass with probabilities 0.8,0.5,0.4. Find probabilities that (a) all pass, (b) all fail, (c) at least one passes, (d) exactly one fails.
problems.idea: Under independence, multiply probabilities for each specific pass/fail pattern and add disjoint patterns.
formulas: For independent events, joint probability is the product; P(at least one)=1-P(none).
steps: Assuming independent outcomes, (a) all pass: 0.8·0.5·0.4=0.16.
(b) All fail: 0.2·0.5·0.6=0.06. Thus (c) at least one passes: 1-0.06=0.94.
Without independence these joint probabilities are not determined. For example, nested pass events can have all-pass probability 0.4 rather than 0.16 with the same individual probabilities.
problems.note: The printed scan gives the individual probabilities but does not explicitly state that the students’ outcomes are independent. The numerical answers above use that additional assumption.

problems.title: Ordered drawing of repeated letter cards
problems.question: Nine cards bear the Georgian letters ი,ი,ი,ე,ხ,ხ,ვ,რ,ც. Draw without replacement and arrange in draw order. Find the probability of (a) ვირი from four draws; (b) ცხვირი from six draws.
problems.idea: Multiply the sequential probabilities, accounting for the remaining copies of repeated letters.
formulas: Without replacement, each next probability uses the remaining desired-letter count divided by the remaining total.
steps: For ვირი, the ordered requirements are ვ,ი,რ,ი. The probability is (1/9)(3/8)(1/7)(2/6)=1/504.
For ცხვირი, the requirements are ც,ხ,ვ,ი,რ,ი. The probability is (1/9)(2/8)(1/7)(3/6)(1/5)(2/4)=1/5040.
The repeated ი cards are distinct cards even though they carry the same letter; this is why their remaining counts matter.

problems.title: A geometric probability for a linear equation
problems.question: For ax=b with 0<a≤6 and 0<b≤10, find the probability that its root exceeds 1.
problems.idea: Under uniform continuous selection, use area in the (a,b) rectangle.
formulas: The root is x=b/a; uniform geometric probability=favourable area/total area.
steps: Since a>0, x>1 iff b>a.
The rectangle has area 6·10=60. The excluded region 0<b≤a≤6 is a right triangle of area 6²/2=18.
The favourable area is 60-18=42, giving probability 42/60=7/10.
problems.note: A probability model must be specified. If a,b instead mean independently uniform positive integers in those ranges, the answer is (9+8+7+6+5+4)/60=13/20.

problems.title: Overlap of a right triangle and its 45-degree rotation
problems.question: An isosceles right triangle has hypotenuse $\sqrt{2\sqrt2-2}$. Rotate it 45° counterclockwise about its right-angle vertex. Find the overlap area.
problems.idea: Scale a coordinate model and split the overlap into two triangles or integrate its straight edges.
formulas: If the equal leg is s, then s²=hypotenuse²/2=√2-1; triangle area=base·height/2.
steps: Put the original triangle at (0,0),(s,0),(0,s). Its inequalities are x≥0,y≥0,x+y≤s.
The rotated triangle adds y≥x and y≤s/√2 inside the original first quadrant.
Up to height s/2 the overlap width is y; from s/2 to s/√2 it is s-y. The two elementary triangle/trapezoid areas total s²(1/√2-1/2).
Substitute s²=√2-1 to obtain (√2-1)²/2=(3-2√2)/2.

problems.title: An angle bisector fixes lengths and angles
problems.question: In ABC, AK is an internal bisector meeting BC, with BK=2,CK=1 and ACK=60°. Find AK and the angles of ABC.
problems.idea: Use the bisector theorem and the cosine rule.
formulas: AB/AC=BK/CK; cosine rule; bisector length squared=bc[1-a²/(b+c)²].
steps: BC=3 and C=60°. Let AC=b. Then AB=2b.
The cosine rule gives (2b)²=b²+9-2·b·3·cos60°=b²+9-3b. Thus b²+b-3=0, so b=(√13-1)/2.
The bisector satisfies AK²=2b²[1-9/(3b)²]=2b²-2=5-√13.
The sine rule gives sinB=sin60°/2=√3/4. Only the acute branch can coexist with C=60°, so B=arcsin(√3/4) and A=120°-B.

problems.title: Probability for a strip inside a trapezoid
problems.question: An isosceles trapezoid has bases 2 and 6 cm and acute angle 30°. Through the diagonal intersection draw a base-parallel section MN. KL is the trapezoid midline. Find the probability that a uniformly random point of the trapezoid lies in strip KMNL.
problems.idea: Use the section heights and lengths; the total height cancels.
formulas: Diagonal intersection divides a trapezoid’s height in its base ratio; parallel section lengths vary linearly; probability=area ratio.
steps: Let the total height be h, measuring upward from the large base. The diagonal intersection is at 6/(6+2)=3/4 of h.
The section there is 6+(2-6)(3/4)=3. The midline KL has length 4 and height h/2.
The strip has height 3h/4-h/2=h/4, so its area is (3+4)(h/4)/2=7h/8.
The whole area is (2+6)h/2=4h. Their ratio is (7h/8)/(4h)=7/32.
problems.note: K,L are the endpoints of the midline. The diagonal intersection itself is unnamed in the scan; keeping these points distinct is necessary to interpret KMNL.
